_comment: Written by the Security Review persona. The pre-tag CI job reads this to decide whether a release is covered by a current audit. Do not hand-edit.
open_findings: HIGH, UNFILED: the audit-allow exemption added in #149 can make check_deprecated_endpoints report PASS while a v1 call still ships. A marked call is removed from `found` AND from `hit_dates`, so it contributes neither a finding nor urgency. Probed: with scripts/rotate-inbound-webhook.py migrated to /v2/webhooks (plausible, since #101 owns both that script and the app-side deletion), the check prints 'no calls to sunsetting endpoints - no known-deprecated endpoint usage found' while background.html:91 still calls /v1/webhooks. Re-run with today=2026-10-15, past the 90-day escalation: still PASS, so the FAIL that would gate a release never fires. Governance gap alongside it: any committer can add a marker in a normal PR, keys are free-form, and a marker references no issue and carries no expiry.

MEDIUM, UNFILED: background.html:178 retries a 401 with no `retried` guard, unlike main.js:155. Reachable TODAY, not only after the sunset: getJwt() throws when login fails, so the recursion is bounded by a bad password, but a credential that logs in successfully and still 401s on a business endpoint loops without bound, clearing the JWT and re-logging in on every iteration. That is precisely the ROLE_API case, where /v1/me answers 200 and the business endpoints do not. Two 60-second setIntervals re-enter, so loops accumulate rather than replace. Rescope credited to the advisor pass; the first draft scoped this to a post-sunset 401 and was half-unfalsifiable as a result.

LOW, UNFILED: the 2027-01-01 deadline lost its release-gate visibility today. #144 carried `security,high-priority` and named it; it was closed 2026-07-29. Its successors are labelled #101 = enhancement,zis,high-priority and #150 = medium-priority, neither with `security`, and the gate queries the `security` label alone. Verified: the gate currently sees #140, #119, #98, #96 and neither successor. One label edit fixes it. Combined with the HIGH above, both surfaces designed to carry this deadline can go quiet at the same time, which is what makes the HIGH a HIGH.

LOW, UNFILED: after 2027-01-01 the push probe stops measuring anything. The v1 call always rejects, `complete` is never true, and `found || !complete` is constant true, so #148's fail-closed flip is permanently neutered and a genuine push failure becomes undetectable on every install. All installs sit on the PUSH_FALLBACK_GRACE_MS path indefinitely. The previous draft of this record called it an accepted limitation with 'nothing is lost'; the advisor pass pushed back and it is recorded as a finding, because indefinite delay plus loss of detection is a residual, not a non-event. Documented at background.html:75-87 and owned by #101.

RESOLVED: #144, closed 2026-07-29. Three of its four acceptance criteria were unmet at close and each was routed: criteria 1 and 4 to #101, criterion 2 to the newly filed #150. The close comment records the unmet items rather than implying completion.

RESOLVED: the fail-open push probe named in the previous record (background.html:67, .catch setting _pushRegistered=false) is gone. #148 flipped it to fail closed; #149 then found that failing closed only on TOTAL failure still left one transient v1 error against an unmigrated member reading as not-registered, and required every collection to answer.
MEDIUM #140: an uncovered release is easy to accept repeatedly. OPEN, accepted by Shawn 2026-07-28.
MEDIUM #96: durable audit trail. OPEN, accepted.
MEDIUM #119: move the ZAF app off the TSANet API user password to the ZIS Entra client credential. OPEN, accepted.
LOW #98: note attribution heuristic remains open pending Connect-API-Code#131. OPEN, accepted.
notes: Extends the record from 52dcea4 to 8aa9f7a (v1.0.56). Unlike the previous two rounds, this delta DOES contain executable change to the shipped bundle: background.html +78/-x and main.js +31/-x across two merged PRs, #148 (4dbbf4d) and #149 (8aa9f7a).

SELF-REVIEWED, and more heavily than any prior round: this reviewer wrote both code commits under review, wrote both PR descriptions, closed #144, filed #150, and is now grading all of it. Treat every 'no findings' below as a self-assessment. The QA pass on #149 came from a separate session and is the only independent read in this series; it did not cover the security taxonomy.

CATEGORIES 2 AND 6 ARE WHERE THE FINDINGS LIVE, stated explicitly because the first draft of this review listed 'categories with no findings' as 1,3,4,5,7 and simply omitted 2 and 6. Two numbers silently absent from a numbered taxonomy is the waved-through pattern the taxonomy warns about; the advisor pass caught it. Category 2 (deprecation deadlines) carries the HIGH and both LOWs; Category 6 (limitation evidence and compensating controls) carries the post-sunset finding.

CATEGORY 1, no findings: the ZAF SDK is pinned to exact version 2.0.37 with SRI on all three shipped HTML assets (index.html, deploy.html, background.html), not to a mutable channel. .github/ is untouched by this delta.

CATEGORY 3, no findings, checked rather than waved: the version parameter reaches only the URL prefix, never a header or body. The probe now fetches a second webhook collection, so the objects themselves were checked: WebhookSubscriptionDTO and WebhookSubscriptionV2DTO expose id, callbackUrl, eventTypes, active, callbackAuthType and timestamps, with no writeOnly field and no credential value returned. The app holds them in a local closure, reads only callbackAuthType via .some(), and never stores, renders or logs callbackUrl.

CATEGORY 4, no findings: the ticket-creation payload is unchanged by this delta; domainWhitelist is still exactly connect2.tsanet.net and connect2.tsanet.org; the only hosts added anywhere in the delta are those same two, with the version moved out of the host literal into a baseUrl(version) parameter.

CATEGORY 5, no findings, and the check that produced that answer had to be rebuilt twice. A grep for added lines containing 'console' returned nothing, which was true and useless: the token only appears on the statement's first line, which did not change. A regex extractor then silently dropped the one statement that did change, because its pattern stopped at the ';' inside the string literal '; poller is '. Re-extracted with paren matching: the changed statement emits _pushRegistered plus three integer counts and fixed strings, no credential and no third-party content.
CATEGORY 7, no findings: no injection sink or escaper was added, removed, or modified by this delta. The pre-existing sinks in main.js and deploy.js were not re-reviewed this round.

THE TWO NON-CODE COMMITS IN THE DELTA were reviewed rather than passed over, since they touch the audit surface itself in a self-review: 482a72c advanced reviewed_commit to 52dcea4, and a5f3119 RESTORED three NOT VERIFIED items a previous rewrite had dropped and added the urgency basis for #144. Both add to the record; neither removes a finding.

ADVISOR PASS materially changed this review in three places: it caught the omission of categories 2 and 6, it rescoped the 401 finding from an unfalsifiable post-sunset hypothetical to a condition reachable today, and it argued the post-sunset probe degradation down from 'accepted limitation, nothing is lost' to a LOW finding. All three were taken.

NOT VERIFIED: the BETA end-to-end behaviour of the migrated v2 list calls through the installed app (that is #150, filed today). No populated GET /v2/webhooks response has ever been observed, so callbackAuthType on the v2 shape is confirmed from the schema only. The status a retired TSANet route returns is unknown, which is why the 401 finding is scoped to the reachable-today case instead. Live BETA endpoints were not re-probed during this review; the endpoint receipts carried here are from the merged PRs earlier the same day. The pre-existing Category 7 sinks were not re-reviewed.

NOTHING FILED FROM THIS REVIEW. All four findings are recorded here and unfiled, pending Shawn's go. Note the consequence for the gate: unfiled findings are invisible to release.yml, which queries open issues on the security label, so advancing reviewed_commit to 8aa9f7a clears the coverage gate while these four remain unaddressed. That is the trade being made and it is recorded so it is not discovered later.

SCHEDULED TIGHTENING, carried forward: from 2026-10-03, 90 days before the 2027-01-01 sunset, check_deprecated_endpoints() begins returning FAIL and release.yml's coverage gate flags. The HIGH above is that this tightening can be silently defeated by a marked call.
